title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
seoTitle: What Is Two-Factor Authentication? Why Businesses Need It
seoDescription: Two-factor authentication adds a second check, such as a code on your phone, when logging in. How it works, which accounts need it first, and options.
summary: Two-factor authentication (2FA) requires a second proof of identity, such as a code from an authenticator app or a security key, in addition to a password. It blocks most account takeovers that use stolen or guessed passwords, which makes it the single most effective security step for business accounts.

dataPoints.label: Methods
dataPoints.value: Authenticator app codes, passkeys and security keys, SMS codes (weakest)

dataPoints.label: Protect first
dataPoints.value: Email, domain and DNS, cloud hosting, accounting, banking, admin panels

dataPoints.label: Recovery
dataPoints.value: Backup codes stored safely, and a second admin on critical accounts

dataPoints.label: For your own software
dataPoints.value: Build 2FA into admin and finance roles from the start

body:
## Why it matters

Most business breaches start with a compromised email or admin account. With 2FA, a stolen password alone is not enough.

## Rolling it out

1. Turn it on for email, domain registrar, cloud and banking accounts.
2. Require it for admin users in your own applications.
3. Store recovery codes securely.

See [cybersecurity basics for founder-led businesses](/blog/cybersecurity-basics-for-founder-led-businesses).

faqs.a: Better than nothing, but authenticator apps and passkeys are more resistant to SIM-swap and phishing attacks.
Only slightly, and most apps remember trusted devices for a period.
